'''Cristoforo Alasia de Quesada''' (1864–1918) was an Italian [[mathematician]].

== Life and work ==
Alasia studied at the universities of Turin (under [[Enrico D'Ovidio]] and [[Giuseppe Peano]]){{sfn | Halsted | 1902 | p=183 }} and Rome (under [[Luigi Cremona]]). In 1893 began his academic career as mathematics professor in different high schools at [[Sassari]], [[Tempio Pausania]], [[Oristano]], [[Ozieri]], [[Brindisi]] and, finally, at [[Albenga]].{{sfn | Fedriani | 1960 | p=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani }}

Alasia was well known at the beginning of 20th century for he was the founder of ''Le Matematiche Pure e Applicate'',{{sfn | Furinghetti | 2012 | p=190 }} a journal devoted to the improvement of scientific knowledge of mathematics teachers.{{sfn | Enea | 2018 | p=395 }}
